discovery: Proposal and foundations of spin qubits in semiconductors for quantum computation

nominees.name: David P. DiVincenzo
nominees.affiliation: RWTH Aachen University and Forschungszentrum Jülich, Germany

nominees.name: Bruce E. Kane
nominees.affiliation: Laboratory for Physical Sciences, University of Maryland, USA

subfield: Quantum information / condensed matter physics (semiconductor spin qubits)
motivation: In 1998 Loss and DiVincenzo showed that single electron spins confined in semiconductor quantum dots, coupled by gate-controlled exchange, could form a universal quantum computer. In the same year Kane proposed encoding qubits in the nuclear and electron spins of individual phosphorus donors in isotopically purified silicon, addressed by surface gates. Together these proposals launched the field of semiconductor spin qubits. They set a clear, demanding programme: isolate, control and read out single spins in solid-state devices built with the tools of the microelectronics industry. Over 25 years, laboratories worldwide have realised that programme. They have achieved single-shot spin readout, fidelities above 99% for one- and two-qubit gates, coherence times of seconds in silicon, and multi-qubit processors. Following the 2025 prize for superconducting circuits, this work stands out as a deep, lasting route from fundamental quantum physics to scalable quantum technology.
